title: Heirloom
summary: California company using limestone to capture atmospheric carbon dioxide.
bodyHtml:
Heirloom accelerates the natural weathering of limestone to absorb CO2, then releases it in a concentrated stream for storage. The process uses widely available material and modular contactors.

The company operates pilot and commercial-scale facilities and sells removals to buyers including Microsoft.

Why it matters

  • Enhanced weathering with limestone
  • Modular contactors
  • Removal contracts

businessMeaning: Using cheap, abundant limestone avoids the sorbent supply constraints of other DAC designs. Energy for regeneration remains the main cost.
investmentLens: Private; a cost-curve bet on carbon removal becoming a real market.
